prompt:
Challenge C036-CH2: Big retailers will stop taking conventional plastic lidding film by 2028; we need a compostable one that still seals.
Detail: Several large

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research on PLA film modifications using wax coatings demonstrates reduced water vapour transmission rates while maintaining compostability certification under EN 13432, directly addressing moisture barrier challenges in refrigerated produce packaging.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03445","field":"abstract","quote":"Both wax types significantly reduced WVTR, with carnauba wax coatings at 15 µm achieving a 63% reduction relative to uncoated PLA. Compostability under industrial conditions was not adversely affected by the wax coating at the tested thicknesses, as confirmed by disintegration testing according to EN 13432."}]},{"text":"Work on nanoclay-modified PLA shows oxygen barrier improvements of 47% through melt compounding at loadings compatible with food contact regulations, providing an alternative approach to enhance gas transmission properties without additional process steps.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03441","field":"abstract","quote":"This study examines the incorporation of organically modified montmorillonite nanoclay at loadings of 1, 3, and 5 wt% into PLA matrices via melt compounding. X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy confirmed an intercalated–exfoliated nanoclay morphology at 3 wt% loading, corresponding to the lowest oxygen transmission rate measured—a reduction of 47% compared to neat PLA. Migration testing according to EU food contact material regulations showed no detectable nanoclay migration into fatty food simulants."}]},{"text":"Development of PLA-thermoplastic starch multilayer structures using compatibilisers achieved improved seal strength and verified compostability within 12 weeks under EN 13432 conditions, demonstrating a coextrusion approach that could enhance seal performance without adhesive layers.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03447","field":"abstract","quote":"A maleic anhydride-grafted PLA compatibiliser was applied at the PLA/TPS interface to improve interlayer adhesion. Peel strength testing confirmed that compatibiliser inclusion increased adhesion energy by 55%. Compostability under industrial conditions (EN 13432) was verified through disintegration and ecotoxicity testing; all formulations passed within the 12-week test period."}]}],"fit":"partial","fitReason":"The researcher's publications address individual components of the challenge—barrier enhancement, compostability certification, and interfacial adhesion in PLA films—but do not directly investigate low-temperature anti-fog performance or heat-seal strength recovery on rPET tooling, which are critical unmet requirements [SYN-PUB-03445, SYN-PUB-03441, SYN-PUB-03447]."}
